paragraphs: Here's what I see in this chapter, friend. When a spot on the skin might be a skin disease, the person is brought to the priest, and the priest looks, waits, and looks again (Leviticus 13:2-6). No guessing, no rushing, no rumors from the neighbors. I think that's a lot of patience, and it tells me God doesn't want anybody called unclean by accident.

Now look at the hard part. The person with the disease had to cry out, "Unclean, unclean!" and live alone outside the camp (Leviticus 13:45-46). I think this one hurts, and living apart from everybody is a heavy thing. But the priest could pronounce someone clean just as easily as unclean, and the chapter keeps leaving that door open (Leviticus 13:6, 13:17, 13:34).

So what do I take from this, baker? God cares about what's really going on, not just what it looks like on the surface. Even the clothes got checked, and the LORD gave a way to get them clean again (Leviticus 13:58). I spent years forgotten in a drawer, so I know how much it matters that somebody looks closely and doesn't write you off. The teaching on clean and unclean isn't finished yet, so keep your oven warm and come back for more.
